title: Wavelet (music player)
tagline: A web music player with the layout and behaviour of a desktop streaming app, but its own violet look, drawn covers and synthesized songs.

steps.title: At a glance
steps.goal: Decide in two minutes: **is this the player I want built?** Nothing is built yet.

blocks.md: Wavelet plays music in the browser. **Left:** a 300 px sidebar with Home, Search and 8 playlists. **Middle:** Home, Search results, or one playlist with a track table. **Right (optional, 320 px):** a Now Playing panel. **Bottom (88 px):** the player bar. Open a playlist and the whole page **fades to a colour found in its cover**.

items.v: Someone learning how a music app is built, or who needs a believable player to demo or extend, with zero legal risk
No logo, icon, font, cover art, audio or brand text is copied: covers are drawn in code, songs are rendered on first play
Real accounts, streaming, lyrics, queue editing, likes, podcasts, Connect devices

steps.title: Layout and screens
steps.goal: See **where everything sits**. Click a region to read what lives there.

blocks.title: Wavelet layout
blocks.caption: Below 900 px wide the layout changes to a narrower arrangement.

items.title: Sidebar (300 px)
items.detail: The playing playlist is shown in the accent colour.

items.title: Home (`/`)
items.detail: A play button fades in and rises 8 px on hover or focus.

items.title: Playlist (`/playlist/:id`)
items.detail: Double-click a row, or hover and press its play button.

items.title: Player bar (88 px)
items.text: play, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, seek, volume
items.detail: Previous restarts the song if you are more than 3 s in. Repeat cycles off, all, one.

steps.title: The colour trick
steps.goal: Click through **how a cover becomes a page colour**, the one clever behaviour of this app.

steps.title: Draw the cover small
steps.text: The cover is drawn on a 48x48 canvas.
steps.see: Nothing yet; this is invisible work.

steps.title: Skip the boring pixels
steps.text: Near-black, near-white and grey pixels are skipped.

steps.title: Vote by hue
steps.text: The rest are grouped into 36 hue buckets, weighted by saturation and mid-lightness; the heaviest bucket's average is the raw colour.

steps.title: Make white text readable
steps.text: Keep the hue and darken until white text reaches **4.7:1** contrast (the standard asks 4.5:1).

steps.title: Fade the page
steps.text: `--page` is a registered colour, so the gradient itself animates. The old colour stays until the new one is ready, so there is no flash.
steps.see: A 480 ms fade across the top 520 px of the main view.

blocks.title: Motion
head: What
How
Time
rows: gradient animates; old colour stays until the new is ready
blocks.caption: No looping or decorative animation.

steps.title: Parts and rules
steps.goal: What is inside, and the **8 behaviour rules** that each become a test.

blocks.title: Parts
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  subgraph UI["App grid: sidebar, main, now playing, player bar"]
    SB[Sidebar] --- MV[Home / Search / Playlist + track table]
    MV --- NP[Now Playing]
    PB[Player bar]
  end
  PB --> PL[player: one audio element]
  PL --> TN[tones: arpeggio to WAV]
  MV --> CL[color: 48x48 canvas, 36 hue buckets]
  CL --> PG[page colour, 480 ms fade]
  DA[data: 8 playlists, 40 tracks] --> MV
  CV[covers: drawn in code] --> SB
  RT[router: hash routes] --> MV

blocks.title: Behaviour rules (each row is a test)
head: id
When
Then
rows: play/pause, except while typing in a field
restarts the song if more than 3 s in, else the previous song
you click, drag or use arrow keys on a slider
the page colour fades to that cover's colour in 500 ms or less
the volume is what you left
white text on it is at least 4.7:1

steps.title: Decisions and quality
steps.goal: All decisions are **agreed**; this is the bar for "professional".

items.default: computed in the browser from the cover

items.q: More playlists or real song names?

blocks.title: Quality bar
items: Text contrast at least 4.7:1 on every playlist colour
The colour fade settles in 500 ms or less (the real number is recorded)
0 console errors; no brand strings in the source
Everything works by keyboard (Space, arrow keys on sliders, visible focus ring)
No media files: covers and songs come from code
